record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical two-dimensional conformal field theory
record.original_question: Give a definition of modular tensor category appropriate for the nonsemisimple setting, prove that the braided tensor category from Conjecture 5.1 has such a nonsemisimple modular tensor category structure, and determine whether such a category still yields a three-dimensional topological quantum field theory and invariants of knots and 3-manifolds.

evidence.quote: Problem 5.2. Give a deﬁnition of modular tensor category in the nonsemisim- ple case and prove that the braided tensor category in Conjecture 5.1 has such a modular tensor category structure. From such a nonsemisimple modular tensor cat- egory, can we still construct a 3-dimensional topological quantum ﬁeld theory and invariants of knots and 3-manifolds?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. A modular tensor category, in the classical (semisimple) sense, is a semisimple braided finite tensor category over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero whose braiding is non-degenerate (equivalently, whose S-matrix is invertible) and which is equipped with a ribbon twist. Such categories are known to give rise via the Reshetikhin–Turaev construction to a three-dimensional topological quantum field theory and to invariants of framed links and closed oriented 3-manifolds.

In the nonsemisimple setting one considers a finite (in the sense of Etingof–Ostrik) braided tensor category C over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, equipped with a ribbon (balancing) structure, but which need not be semisimple. A typical source of such categories is the representation category of a finite-dimensional ribbon (quasi-)Hopf algebra, or the category of modules over a suitable vertex operator algebra associated with a logarithmic two-dimensional conformal field theory.

Concretely, fix a vertex operator algebra V satisfying suitable finiteness and C_2-cofiniteness hypotheses (so that its module category C = Rep(V) is a finite braided tensor category with a natural ribbon twist coming from L_0), and assume C is not semisimple.

The problem.
(a) Formulate a precise definition of "modular tensor category" that applies in the nonsemisimple setting, generalizing the classical definition (i.e., specify what nondegeneracy condition replaces invertibility of the S-matrix, what finiteness/ribbon/unimodularity hypotheses are imposed, and how the various equivalent classical formulations should be unified or chosen).

(b) Show that the finite ribbon braided tensor category C = Rep(V) above carries the structure of a nonsemisimple modular tensor category in the sense of part (a).

(c) Determine whether a nonsemisimple modular tensor category, in the sense of part (a), gives rise to a three-dimensional topological quantum field theory and to invariants of framed knots/links and closed oriented 3-manifolds, and if so construct such a TQFT and invariants.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made on all three parts. A definition of nonsemisimple modular tensor category (finite ribbon braided tensor category with non-degenerate braiding, often unimodular) is now standard, formalized notably by Shimizu and others. The vertex-operator-algebra side (modularity of Rep(V) for suitable C_2-cofinite V) has been established by Huang, McRae, and collaborators. The construction of 3d TQFTs and 3-manifold/link invariants from such categories has been carried out by De Renzi, Gainutdinov, Geer, Patureau-Mirand, and Runkel, including 2+1 TQFT extensions via modified traces. Some refinements (e.g. full extension, gluing properties, comparison with logarithmic CFT correlators) remain active research.

status_evidence.title: 3-Dimensional TQFTs from non-semisimple modular categories
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of 3d TQFTs from non-semisimple modular categories using modified traces, renormalizing Lyubashenko's invariants and upgrading them to 2+1-TQFTs.
status_evidence.claim: 3d TQFTs and 3-manifold invariants have been constructed from nonsemisimple modular tensor categories.

status_evidence.title: Non-semisimple TFT and Logarithmic CFT (Hamburg 2018)
status_evidence.snippet: Research program on nonsemisimple TQFTs and their links to logarithmic CFT.
status_evidence.claim: The connection between nonsemisimple modular categories, logarithmic CFT, and TQFTs is an active and developed research area.

status_evidence.title: Unit inclusion in a (nonsemisimple) braided tensor category
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on nonsemisimple braided tensor categories and their modular structure.
status_evidence.claim: Definitions of modularity in the nonsemisimple setting have been formulated and studied.
